Subject: Dedicated GPU capacity — readiness deep-dive & fallback coordination

Hi Eric —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our call, we should schedule a technical deep-dive focused on dedicated GPU pool sizing, autoscaling behaviors under sustained burst, and tenant isolation/failover plans so your infra team can validate we meet ScaleTech's latency and isolation SLOs.

Proposed agenda (45–60 min):
- 10 min: introductions + goals (you + Redwood SME list)
- 20 min: pool topology & sizing logic (Marcus)
- 15 min: autoscale policies, canary & rollback paths (Karthik)
- 10 min: isolation testing and failover scenarios + Q&A (Marissa)

Suggested windows (PT):
- Wednesday Jan 20 — 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00
- Thursday Jan 21 — 09:00–10:00 or 13:00–14:00

Can you confirm preferred slot and which ScaleTech engineers will join? I attached a short runbook and a draft mutual action plan to help guide the discussion.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v1.pdf, mutual_action_plan-draft.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear agenda. Thursday Jan 21 09:00–10:00 PT works best for us. I will have our infra lead (Ava) plus our SRE (internal) join. Our primary asks for the session:
- Deep dive on autoscale policy thresholds and how they behave with long KV cache sessions
- Isolation testing plan (noisy-tenant scenarios) and SLA impact modeling
- Fallback/rollover steps if a pool hits a capacity plateau (we’ll need exact RTO/RPO expectations)

Couple of prep notes from our side: we’ll share a short traffic sample and expected QPS distribution by EOD today.
